addGuests.handler.ts:44 vs :55 — NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN discriminate before/after authz on a sequential integer id, giving a free booking-id enumeration oracle across all tenants

addGuests.handler.ts:52 — authz keyed on mutable session `user.email` string, not a durable `userId` relation on the attendee row; also case-sensitive, so `User@corp.com` denies the legitimate `user@corp.com` session

addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`/`.min(1)` and the route has no rate limiting; one authenticated call can write N attendee rows and fan out N genuine invitation emails with attacker-authored booking title/description via unthrottled `Promise.all` — spam relay + mail-reputation damage

attendee-add-guests-email.ts:19 — `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`` concatenates an unquoted, booking-form-supplied display name into an address header; nodemailer's addressparser splits on unquoted top-level commas, so a name of `evil@attacker.com,` can add a recipient (CRLF injection is not reachable — nodemailer normalizes; the comma path is the realistic one)
Authorization logic bug**

addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` uses AND while the name says OR. Either the branch is unsatisfiable (one role per membership) or it collapses to owner-only; either way every team ADMIN is denied. The codebase already has `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` (BookingListItem.tsx:546) that this ignores

addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 — `teamId ?? 0` feeds a fabricated sentinel resource id into an authz predicate instead of short-circuiting on `!teamId`; also costs two sequential membership round-trips on every personal booking that can only return false

addGuests.handler.ts:71 vs :77 — blacklist is `.toLowerCase()`'d but compared against the RAW `guest`; `Victim@corp.com` defeats `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=victim@corp.com` entirely. Entries are also never `.trim()`ed, so `a@x.com, b@y.com` leaves ` b@y.com` permanently unmatchable

addGuests.handler.ts:70 — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is invented by this change (appears nowhere else in the tree), undocumented, no default, no format validation, and unrequested by the task. Whether it is registered in turbo.json `globalEnv` is UNVERIFIABLE here (turbo.json absent) — if not, Turborepo drops it and the control silently evaluates to `[]`

addGuests.handler.ts:76 — attendee dedup is case-sensitive, so `Victim@corp.com` re-adds an existing `victim@corp.com`; this also always yields non-empty `uniqueGuests`, bypassing the :80 empty-set guard and enabling an unbounded re-send loop that mails every existing attendee each iteration

addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 — the submitted array is never deduped against ITSELF server-side; `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` reaches `createMany` with no `skipDuplicates`, inserting duplicate attendee rows. The uniqueness invariant exists only in a client `refine()` a non-browser caller never runs

addGuests.handler.ts:26→92 — TOCTOU: `findFirst` reads attendees, dedup runs in app memory, a separate `update` writes; no transaction, no `skipDuplicates`, no isolation. Concurrent requests both insert — or, if a UNIQUE constraint exists, the loser throws an unhandled P2002 as a 500

addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `updateCalendarAttendees` runs AFTER the DB commit, outside the try/catch (which wraps only emails at :167). On calendar failure the guests persist but the client gets an error, and RETRY IS PERMANENTLY BROKEN: the guests are now attendees, so `uniqueGuests` is empty and :80 throws "Emails must be unique and valid"
addGuests.handler.ts:22 — no idempotency key, no webhook, no booking-history/audit record for an attendee-roster mutation

addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` + `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` use the CALLER's calendar credentials, not the organizer's. The organizer's credentials are eagerly loaded at :38 and never referenced (CONFIRMED — grep shows zero uses of booking.user.credentials). When an attendee or team admin adds a guest, the calendar patch runs with a token that doesn't own the event

addGuests.handler.ts:168 — passes raw `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`, to `sendAddGuestsEmails`; email-manager.ts:541 then classifies an already-existing attendee whose address was resubmitted as "new" and sends them a full booking-confirmation email + fresh ICS REQUEST instead of the add-guests notice

email-manager.ts:525 — `sendAddGuestsEmails` is the ONLY sender in the file taking no `eventTypeMetadata` and never calling `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`; sibling `sendLocationChangeEmails` (:495) gates at :503 and :515 (CONFIRMED — read both). Event types configured to suppress email still emit

email-manager.ts:539 — the map iterates ALL attendees, so adding one guest re-sends a `method:REQUEST` ICS to every pre-existing attendee; volume is O(total attendees), not O(new guests)

organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — `replyTo: [organizer, ...all attendee emails]` leaks the full guest roster in a header to every team-member copy, and any casual reply broadcasts to all guests; the sibling written in this same diff (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:21) uses organizer only

addGuests.handler.ts:26,92 — no guard on `booking.status` (CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING) and none on `endTime < now`; both new templates then emit `status: "CONFIRMED"` / `method: "REQUEST"`, re-materializing a cancelled event on the guest's calendar

BookingListItem.tsx:194 — the action is appended unconditionally to `editBookingActions`, rendered for past bookings at :553 and :554 (CONFIRMED — read both); "Add guests" is offered on finished bookings with no server-side time guard

BookingListItem.tsx:246 — `bookedActions` drops `edit_booking` wholesale on the Recurring tab (CONFIRMED), so "Add guests" is unreachable from the UI for recurring bookings and no alternative entry point was added

addGuests.handler.ts:138 — `recurringEvent` is parsed into `evt` but the update targets a single row; a guest added to a series lands on exactly one occurrence, with no "this event / all events" choice

addGuests.handler.ts:145 — `seatsPerTimeSlot` is copied into `evt` but never guarded; attendees are inserted with no BookingSeat/referenceUid row, so on seated events the new rows are invisible to seat-based cancel/reschedule paths
addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `videoCallData` is assembled but no video adapter is invoked; Zoom/Meet participant lists are never updated

addGuests.handler.ts:58 — `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`: the `|| 0` guarantees a miss rather than short-circuiting, so a null-userId booking throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError as an untranslated 500 — and AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 renders that raw ORM message in a toast

addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` discards the bound `err`, uses console.log for an error, and still returns success. This package imports a real logger (email-manager.ts:10) — and this is exactly the signal that would reveal the mass-mail abuse above
common.json:2434 — new `add_emails` ("Add Emails") sits beside pre-existing `add_email` ("Add Email") at :2433, differing only in plurality

_router.tsx:79 — only `addGuests` exists; no remove/list endpoint and no UI to remove an already-added guest, so "guest management" ships add-only and an accidental addition is unrecoverable through the product

One candidate finding was checked and disproved** (flagging it so it isn't re-raised): `t("additional_guests")` resolves to `"Add guests"` (common.json:580), which reads as an action and is consistent with sibling `"Edit location"`. The *key name* is a noun phrase, but the rendered label is correct in both the menu and the dialog title.

Not confirmable either way, and no lens should be read as having settled them: whether `Attendee(bookingId,email)` has a UNIQUE constraint; whether `Booking.userId` is nullable; the real semantics of `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner`; what `bookingsProcedure` actually enforces; whether a shared CalendarEvent builder exists that the 24-line inline `evt` literal should reuse; whether sibling mutations fire webhooks; whether `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is registered in `turbo.json` `globalEnv`; and whether icon names `"user-plus"`/`"triangle-alert"` exist in this repo's icon set (`triangle-alert` is the lucide ≥0.400 rename of `alert-triangle`, so it is version-dependent and worth a one-line check against the full tree).
No SSRF and no SQL/NoSQL/command injection were found — all queries go through parameterized Prisma, and there is no `$queryRaw`, `exec`, `spawn`, or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:52 — `isAttendee` (email string match) is accepted as authority to MUTATE the attendee list; every guest can add unlimited third parties to someone else's booking, and each added address becomes an attendee who can add more — a transitive, organizer-invisible invite chain

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization is granted if `isAttendee` is true (`booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`), and the mutation then performs `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` to add arbitrary new attendee emails. Because the handler re-reads attendees from the DB each call, any newly added guest becomes an attendee and will satisfy `isAttendee` on later calls, enabling a transitive “guest can invite more guests” chain. There is also no limit/role restriction on how many emails can be added in one call beyond basic email-format validation. The “organizer-invisible” part is overstated (the handler sends organizer/team notification emails), but the core issue—attendees being allowed to mutate the attendee list and creating transitive invite authority—is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:26 — `findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` is fully unscoped on an attacker-supplied PK; any authenticated user materializes any booking in the deployment (incl. `references` and organizer `credentials`) before any authz runs

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first fetches `booking` via `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees, eventType, destinationCalendar, references, user: { include: { destinationCalendar, credentials }}}})` before performing any authorization checks. Since `bookingId` is attacker-supplied and the query is only scoped by `id`, any authenticated caller can cause the server to load arbitrary bookings (and their `references` plus organizer `user.credentials`) into memory prior to the `FORBIDDEN` check. While the handler does not return those fields, it still enables booking-id existence probing (NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN) and unnecessarily retrieves highly sensitive data before authz.

addGuests.handler.ts:44 vs :55 — NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN discriminate before/after authz on a sequential integer id, giving a free booking-id enumeration oracle across all tenants

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code first fetches a booking by sequential integer `id` without any authorization scoping (`findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })`). It then throws `NOT_FOUND` if no record exists, but throws `FORBIDDEN` if the booking exists and the caller is not an organizer/attendee/(team admin+owner). This difference in error code/message makes it possible for any authenticated user to probe arbitrary booking IDs and learn which IDs exist (an enumeration oracle across teams/tenants), because existence is checked before authz and the response distinguishes the two cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:52 — authz keyed on mutable session `user.email` string, not a durable `userId` relation on the attendee row; also case-sensitive, so `User@corp.com` denies the legitimate `user@corp.com` session

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the attendee authorization path is `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` which relies on exact, case-sensitive string equality against the session email. The diff also shows attendee rows being created with only `{ name, email, timeZone, locale }` (no durable userId link), so access can break if the session email differs by case (e.g., `User@corp.com` vs `user@corp.com`) or if a user’s email changes after the booking. This is a concrete correctness/authz fragility introduced/used in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`/`.min(1)` and the route has no rate limiting; one authenticated call can write N attendee rows and fan out N genuine invitation emails with attacker-authored booking title/description via unthrottled `Promise.all` — spam relay + mail-reputation damage

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)`/`.max(...)` bound in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and the handler uses `createMany` to insert one attendee row per email and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which builds an array of per-attendee email sends and executes them via `Promise.all(...)` without any cap. This makes the number of DB writes and outbound emails directly proportional to an attacker-controlled array size in a single authenticated request, enabling abuse (spam/fan-out/DoS) by any user who is organizer/attendee/(team admin/owner) of a booking. While broader platform rate limiting could exist elsewhere, there is no limiting visible in this route/handler and the unbounded fan-out is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: attendee-add-guests-email.ts:19 — `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`` concatenates an unquoted, booking-form-supplied display name into an address header; nodemailer's addressparser splits on unquoted top-level commas, so a name of `evil@attacker.com,` can add a recipient (CRLF injection is not reachable — nodemailer normalizes; the comma path is the realistic one)
Authorization logic bug**

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...));` but the name and typical intent imply an OR condition. Using `&&` requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner, which will incorrectly deny access to users who are only one of those (admin-only or owner-only). This is a concrete authorization logic bug introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` uses AND while the name says OR. Either the branch is unsatisfiable (one role per membership) or it collapses to owner-only; either way every team ADMIN is denied. The codebase already has `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` (BookingListItem.tsx:546) that this ignores
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner incorrectly requires both roles, denying admins; it should be || (admin OR owner).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 — `teamId ?? 0` feeds a fabricated sentinel resource id into an authz predicate instead of short-circuiting on `!teamId`; also costs two sequential membership round-trips on every personal booking that can only return false

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the authz flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. This does pass a fabricated `teamId` of `0` into the team membership predicates when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null/undefined, rather than short-circuiting when there is no team context. That is verifiable in the diff and can lead to incorrect authorization semantics if `0` is ever meaningful in those queries, and it also guarantees at least one unnecessary membership lookup for non-team (personal) bookings. The finding’s performance wording is slightly overstated: due to `&&` short-circuiting, the second call won’t run if the first returns false, so it’s not necessarily “two” round-trips on every personal booking, but the sentinel-id issue and wasted lookup are real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:76 — attendee dedup is case-sensitive, so `Victim@corp.com` re-adds an existing `victim@corp.com`; this also always yields non-empty `uniqueGuests`, bypassing the :80 empty-set guard and enabling an unbounded re-send loop that mails every existing attendee each iteration

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the deduplication/filtering for `uniqueGuests` compares raw strings: it checks `guest === attendee.email` and compares against a lowercased blacklist, but it never normalizes `guest` or `attendee.email` to a consistent case. Email local-parts are typically treated case-insensitively in practice, so `Victim@corp.com` would not match an existing `victim@corp.com` attendee and would be treated as “unique”, allowing a duplicate attendee record to be created and the empty-set guard (uniqueGuests.length===0) to be bypassed in that case. The finding’s ‘unbounded re-send loop’ phrasing is overstated (there’s no loop in code), but repeated calls could indeed trigger repeated sends to all attendees via `sendAddGuestsEmails` once a new “unique” (case-variant) guest is accepted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 — the submitted array is never deduped against ITSELF server-side; `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` reaches `createMany` with no `skipDuplicates`, inserting duplicate attendee rows. The uniqueness invariant exists only in a client `refine()` a non-browser caller never runs
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate points out that the server does not deduplicate duplicates within the submitted guest email array, so repeated emails (e.g., ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]) can reach createMany and insert duplicate attendee rows (and notes lack of skipDuplicates / reliance on client-side validation). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:26→92 — TOCTOU: `findFirst` reads attendees, dedup runs in app memory, a separate `update` writes; no transaction, no `skipDuplicates`, no isolation. Concurrent requests both insert — or, if a UNIQUE constraint exists, the loser throws an unhandled P2002 as a 500

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first reads the booking (including attendees) via prisma.booking.findFirst, then computes uniqueGuests in application memory, then performs a separate prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany. Because there is no transaction/locking and createMany is not using skipDuplicates, two concurrent addGuests calls can both observe the same initial attendees and both attempt to insert the same guest emails. That can lead to duplicated attendee rows (if no DB uniqueness constraint) or a Prisma unique constraint error (e.g., P2002) bubbling up as an unhandled server error since the update is not caught/translated to a TRPCError. This is a verifiable TOCTOU/concurrency correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `updateCalendarAttendees` runs AFTER the DB commit, outside the try/catch (which wraps only emails at :167). On calendar failure the guests persist but the client gets an error, and RETRY IS PERMANENTLY BROKEN: the guests are now attendees, so `uniqueGuests` is empty and :80 throws "Emails must be unique and valid"

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation updates the booking attendees in the DB via prisma.booking.update (commit happens before any external side effects), then calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no try/catch or transaction rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation will error after the DB has already persisted the new attendees. On a subsequent retry with the same guest emails, the initial booking fetch will now include those attendees, causing `uniqueGuests` to be empty and the handler to throw `BAD_REQUEST` at the `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0)` check, making retries fail. The existing try/catch only wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails`, not the calendar update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:22 — no idempotency key, no webhook, no booking-history/audit record for an attendee-roster mutation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `addGuests` mutation/handler, and it indeed does not implement an idempotency key, emit a webhook, or write a booking-history/audit record. The finding is therefore a process/product expectation rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` + `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` use the CALLER's calendar credentials, not the organizer's. The organizer's credentials are eagerly loaded at :38 and never referenced (CONFIRMED — grep shows zero uses of booking.user.credentials). When an attendee or team admin adds a guest, the calendar patch runs with a token that doesn't own the event

adjudication.rationale: The handler authorizes not only the organizer but also any attendee or team admin/owner (`isAttendee` check) to call `addGuestsHandler`. However, the calendar update is performed with credentials derived from the *caller* (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });` where `user` is `ctx.user`). The booking query eagerly loads `booking.user.credentials` (organizer’s credentials) but they are never referenced afterwards, matching the finding. This means when a non-organizer adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run under credentials that likely do not own the organizer’s calendar event, causing failures or unintended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:168 — passes raw `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`, to `sendAddGuestsEmails`; email-manager.ts:541 then classifies an already-existing attendee whose address was resubmitted as "new" and sends them a full booking-confirmation email + fresh ICS REQUEST instead of the add-guests notice

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the server correctly filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees/blacklisted) and only persists `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the *raw* input list. In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which template to send; therefore any attendee whose email was resubmitted (already existed, thus not actually “new”) will still match `includes` and be treated as a new guest, receiving `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full booking confirmation/ICS) instead of the add-guests notice. This is a verifiable logic defect introduced by passing `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:525 — `sendAddGuestsEmails` is the ONLY sender in the file taking no `eventTypeMetadata` and never calling `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`; sibling `sendLocationChangeEmails` (:495) gates at :503 and :515 (CONFIRMED — read both). adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:531 — the `calendarEvent.team?.members` fan-out is dead code: the handler's `evt` literal (:124-147) never sets `team` and the booking query never includes `eventType.team`, so team co-hosts are never notified — even though the handler explicitly authorizes team admins/owners

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:539 — the map iterates ALL attendees, so adding one guest re-sends a `method:REQUEST` ICS to every pre-existing attendee; volume is O(total attendees), not O(new guests)
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

The candidate doesn’t mention the specific newGuests.includes(attendee.email) detail, but it describes the same behavioral bug (emailing all attendees when only new guests should be handled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — `replyTo: [organizer, ...all attendee emails]` leaks the full guest roster in a header to every team-member copy, and any casual reply broadcasts to all guests; the sibling written in this same diff (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:21) uses organizer only

This will embed the full attendee/guest email list in the Reply-To header of the organizer/team-member notification email (the `to` is a single team member, but they can see the full reply-to list) and makes a normal “reply”/“reply-all” likely to broadcast to all attendees. adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` indexes without optional chaining AND interpolates a different value than the sibling template does for the same subject key; since guests are created with `name: ""`, a handler-created guest at index 0 yields `Guests Added: <type> with  at <date>`

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:58 — `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`: the `|| 0` guarantees a miss rather than short-circuiting, so a null-userId booking throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError as an untranslated 500 — and AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 renders that raw ORM message in a toast

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44 — `message` is a template literal and always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable; the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` key (common.json:1137) can never render

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:37 — success toast says "Guests added" unconditionally; the server silently drops already-attending and blacklisted addresses and returns no count. Submit 5, have 4 dropped, and the UI reports unqualified success

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-41 — `onSuccess` never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`; only Cancel (:91) clears it, so reopening after an error-then-success shows a stale red banner over an empty form

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — deleting every row leaves `[]` and `handleAdd` returns silently with no toast or message; the Add button appears dead
